correctness.rationale: For a specified center and k selected pendant labels, deletion is a bijection onto all labeled trees on the m=n-k residual labels, with one tree if m=1. Thus every marked event has positive and equal probability and E S_(k,n)=n binom(n-1,k) tau(m)/n^(n-2). Reattaching makes the center a nonleaf; the other residual leaves are precisely noncenter labels absent from the uniform length-(m-2) Prüfer word. Joint absence of j designated labels has probability ((m-j)/m)^(m-2), so expansion in z-1 gives the displayed Palm PGF. At m=2 the empty word contributes one noncenter leaf; at m=1 there are only the k marked leaves. Summing over marked events identifies the Palm mean minus n p_n with normalized covariance. The initial gap is Var(L_n)/E L_n>0 by the star and path for n>=4. For m>=3, p_m<p_(m-1)<=1: the derivative of (x-2) log(1-1/x) is less than -1/(x(x-1)) for x>2, and the function extends continuously to x=2. Hence H(m)-H(m-1)=p_(m-1)+(m-1)(p_m-p_(m-1))<1, whereas H(2)-H(1)=1. This gives exactly the single terminal equality, and explains why it corresponds to stars. Finally p_m=e^(-1)(1+3/(2m)+O(m^-2)); for fixed k the two factors in covariance are n exp(-k)/k!+O_k(1) and k-(k+1)/e+O_k(1/n). Replay: frozen RESULT.md lines 43–95. The verification script was inspected but not executed; no finite check is used for the universal claim.

value.rationale: The exact finite comparison answers how the conditional leaf-count enhancement changes with the degree of bouquet marking, rather than just whether pairs give enhancement. It distinguishes strict gain for every smaller increment from saturation at the star boundary; the covariance coefficients and vacancy counts alone are not the value justification. This is a modest structural result for a natural Palm ordering.
